  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION

Monday, December 13, 2021  7:00 PM  Teleconference

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that a Special Meeting of the Park & Activities Commission of the City of
Rolling Hills Estates will be held on Monday, December 13, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. via Video Teleconference. The
agenda for the special meeting with the items to be discussed is set forth below.

  Posted by the office of Community Services on Thursday, December 9, 2021

Public Participation Information
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) and City Council Resolution No. 2487, due to the
  continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat
  of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being held remotely via teleconference. There will not be a physical
  location for this meeting. Members of the public may participate in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1 669 900 6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 825 1551 9666 Meeting Password: 355733. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 825 1551 9666, Meeting Password: 355733. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION SPECIAL MEETING
  DECEMBER 13, 2021

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates was called to order at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
  Executive Order N-29-20.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope,
  Retz, Romanelli

  Commissioners Absent:  None

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Daniel A-Haja

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT
  MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 15, 2021

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked to clarify the statement in item 6B by Lyneigh
  Palacios asking where the respondents live and where they will be walking from.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ joined the meeting at 7:05 P.M.

  CHAIR POPE noted the question states if the survey asks their street, does it
  show how far they are from the area.

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis clarified if the survey considered walkable
  distances as to why the survey asked for streets or does it consider those further
  away. The survey addresses both but can be clarified further and will replay the
  recording to make sure.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
DECEMBER 13, 2021
   COMMISSIONER BAIN recalled Ms. Palacios asking for addresses and where
  the survey respondents live and understood the intention but may need it
  clarified in minutes.

  CHAIR POPE noted staff will make the changes.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK wanted to clarify his statement in taking out
  the men’s lockers if they are not being used and replacing them with additional
  restroom facilities.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  RETZ to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 15, 2021 WITH REVISIONS.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  CHANDLER PARK PLAYGROUND REVISED SURVEY

  Assistant City Manager Davis (ACM) Davis provided a review of the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA commended staff on their efforts on the survey.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN suggested moving question 5 after question 2 to get more
  answers back from respondents and noted that an alternative is to have survey
  takers go to question 3 from 2F. She also noted that number 8 for question 8 should
  be removed from the sentence it is in front of as it is informational and should
  instead be placed by the question itself. She added that question 9 should state “If
  you answered, ‘yes’ to question 8 above, “and that question 10 should state “If you
  answered ‘no’ to question 8 above”.

  Community Member Mr. Oldroyd from Ranchview stated question 8 does not
  include the ADA requirements as part of the 30ft. x 40ft. playground size. He would
  like clarification as to why the past playground proposal was rejected and if it was
  applicable to the discussion today. Mrs. Oldroyd noted mentioning whether or not
  the ADA requirements will expand the playground footprint on the survey.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 13, 2021
   ACM Davis clarified that the only ADA component is the path to the playground.
  The 30ft. x 40ft. footprint is for the play area; the ADA work would consist of a
  pathway to the play area itself. Restroom access may not be included as it could
  be located closer to the play area through portable units. Mrs. Oldroyd would like
  the survey to note that the ADA pathway may take away trees affecting the
  greenspace of the park.

  CHAIR POPE clarified that a City-wide plan is in place for ADA compliance at all
  parks regardless of play structure. This project would entail moving forward quicker
  to meet ADA standards but the City does plan to meet ADA requirements at all
  parks. ACM Davis added that there is a plan for a pathway to the park already in
  place but would be extended to the play area if approved.

  Community Member Mrs. Oldroyd asked if there would be pathways within the play
  area. ACM Davis clarified that the 30ft. x 40ft. play area will not need pathways
  connecting the play structures as the entire area will be ADA accessible, likely with
  engineered wood chips.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the ADA plan for parks may need to be
  attached to the current project or if the ADA project would stand alone; this way the
  particulars to the play equipment would not include other complexities from the
  overall project.

  ACM Davis noted that the past Commissions did not conduct formal studies on the
  proposed play area at Chandler Park but was reviewed and denied by the past
  Commission. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA confirmed that notion. ACM Davis
  would be glad to share past information as the request came from community
  members in the past.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION WITH CHANGES AND PROCEED
  WITH LAUNCHING THE SURVEY IN JANUARY.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  B.  PARADE OF LIGHTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the event was a success with a
  higher turnout than expected. Some gaps between units were expected in the
  parade and staff will be working with the consultant on closing them in the future.
  About 55 groups participated this year and 13 sponsors supported the event with
  Malaga Bank being the major sponsor at a donation of $1,000. The Promenade on
  the Peninsula provided a Santa this year as well.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 13, 2021
   CHAIR POPE confirmed the positive feedback from the parade and thanked staff
  for another great event.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ was surprised by the outcome and was pleased with the
  Grand Marshal.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked what community outreach was done to bring groups
  into the City. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted Event Brite and social
  media channels were used to promote the event. ACM Davis noted the participants
  are confirmed through Pageantry Parades, the City’s consultant, print
  advertisements in PV News and school flyers were also sent out. Community
  Services Supervisor Pinuelas also noted printed flyers were distributed to local
  grocery stores.

  C.  NEW PROGRAM PROPOSAL- SOUTH BAY MUSIC TOGETHER

  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja provided a brief overview of the staff
  report.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ agree with the program and supports music programs in
  the City.

  CHAIR POPE agreed with COMMISSIONER RETZ and supported adding
  programs to Ernie Howlett Park. She asked if this program would be promoted like
  the other recreation programs.  Community Services Coordinator A-Haja
  responded that it would.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to:

  ACCEPT STAFF RECOMMENDATION AND APPROVE THE ADDITION
  OF THE SOUTH BAY MUSIC TOGETHER PROGRAM AS A CITY
  RECREATION CLASS.

  AYES: Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Persichina, Pope, Retz,
  Romanelli

  The motion carries.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 13, 2021
   A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted that a rail was down at Chandler Park. ACM
  Davis noted the issue and will report to maintenance

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked the age group of the soccer players at Ernie
  Howlett. Community Services Coordinator A-Haja responded that it would be
  AYSO age which is no more than 12. CHAIR POPE confirmed that the ages are
  about 8 to 9 years old.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted that Dapplegray Park looks wonderful.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  CHAIR POPE asked about a past art class at Ernie Howlett. Community Services
  Coordinator A-Haja noted the class was run by the college student instructors for
  one session only. ACM Davis noted the class had a good turnout but could not
  continue due to the instructors’ school obligations.

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK wanted to see more community service or benefit
  events for 2022. Park beautification or community charitable fair to allow people to
  volunteer for local organizations. CHAIR POPE likes the idea and thinks it can be
  accomplished in different forms. COMMISSIONER BAIN volunteered to help
  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK with any subcommittee matters for this. ACM
  Davis noted staff will come forward with a list of events for 2022 and will add a
  charity event to that list for discussion.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas noted the house decorating contest is on
  now, tomorrow is last day to sign up for the contest. Judges will be sent information
  on scoring. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how many houses have signed
  up for the contest. Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas responded that so far
  6 houses have signed up.

  Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas stated the Hills Are Alive Rerun, virtual
  event, will begin this Saturday thru the 31st.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  None

  9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF NOVEMBER 9, 2021

  Received and filed.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 13, 2021
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the maintenance staff lunch is confirmed for
  the December 14 at 11:30am and an email was sent to Commissioners regarding
  contributing.

  CHAIR POPE stated appreciation to COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI for
  coordinating the lunch.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  NATURE CENTER

  None

  B.  PICKLEBALL USAGE

  None

  C.  TENNIS COURT RENOVATION

  None

  D.  PETER WEBER CONTRACT RENEWAL

  None

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked for an update on Butcher Park. ACM
  Davis responded the City is in contract with Wildan and the landscape architect
  and moving forward with specifications. He asked when the project is expected to
  take place. ACM Davis noted the project is budgeted for this year, however there
  are still some items being worked through once again with Metropolitan Water
  District.
  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted the planned installation of additional charging
  stations at City Hall and Ernie Howlett Park. ACM Davis mentioned the approval
  of charging stations at City Hall under the Southern California Edison Charge
  Ready program and the plan on having 2 dual port charging stations at Ernie
  Howlett Park from a past grant.

  11.  ADJOURNMENT

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 13, 2021
   ACM Davis noted to the Commission that the following meeting will take place on
  a Tuesday due to the observance of the Martin Luther King Jr. Holiday taking place
  on Monday that week.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated it was a pleasure working with everyone in
  2021 and wished everyone a happy holiday.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA moved, seconded  by  COMMISSIONER
  MCCORMICK, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:56 PM TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JANUARY 18, 2021
  AT 7:00 P.M., WHICH BE HELD VIA TELECONFERENCE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR POPE so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Daniel A-Haja  Lisa Van Ingen Pope
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
DECEMBER 13, 2021
